1.All:
# Forecasters do the best they can, but sometimes they underestimate or
# overestimate the probability that a storm system will cause a tornado. We
# are interested in how these miscalculations might influence your trust in
# future forecasts. Again, imagine that it is a Saturday morning at 8:00 AM
# and you see this forecast: 20x more likely then 15% chance. As the day
# progresses, imagine that you see some rain and lightning, but the storm
# does not produce a tornado with 25 miles of your residence. How would
# this influence your trust in future forecasts?
#
# WxDash, the IPPRA Extreme Weather and Society Project. Rebuilds this
# chart from the released wave files and nothing else.
# Severe Weather (WX), WX22.
# Version shown to this part of the sample: 20x more likely then 15% chance (`rand_clim_format`).

library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)

# This question was split-sampled - respondents did not all read the
# same thing - so this version is estimated on its own. Pooling the
# versions would average across the treatment.

# Read as character: a question asked in one wave is empty in the
# others, and a column empty for its first thousand rows is guessed
# logical, which turns every real value after it into NA.
wx22 <- read_csv("WX22_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

d <- bind_rows(
  wx22 |>
    filter(rand_clim_format == "1") |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      resp = cond_risk_trust
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp), !is.na(PERSON_WEIGHT))

est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = 1, weights = PERSON_WEIGHT) |>
  group_by(resp) |>
  summarise(p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
            .groups = "drop")

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("It would strongly reduce my trust",
                 "It would reduce my trust",
                 "It would have no effect on my trust",
                 "It would increase my trust",
                 "It would strongly increase my trust")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "Forecasters do the best they can, but sometimes they",
      "underestimate or overestimate the probability that a storm",
      "system will cause a tornado. We are interested in how these",
      "miscalculations might influence your trust in future",
      "forecasts. Again, imagine that it is a Saturday morning at",
      "8:00 AM and you see this forecast: 20x more likely then 15%",
      "chance. As the day progresses, imagine that you see some",
      "rain and lightning, but the storm does not produce a",
      "tornado with 25 miles of your residence. How would this",
      "influence your trust in future forecasts?"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

10.survey_year:
# Forecasters do the best they can, but sometimes they underestimate or
# overestimate the probability that a storm system will cause a tornado. We
# are interested in how these miscalculations might influence your trust in
# future forecasts. Again, imagine that it is a Saturday morning at 8:00 AM
# and you see this forecast: 15% chance then 500x more likely. As the day
# progresses, imagine that you see some rain and lightning, but the storm
# does not produce a tornado with 25 miles of your residence. How would
# this influence your trust in future forecasts?
#
# WxDash, the IPPRA Extreme Weather and Society Project. Rebuilds this
# chart from the released wave files and nothing else.
# Severe Weather (WX), WX22.
# Split by survey year (the `survey_year` column).
# Version shown to this part of the sample: 15% chance then 500x more likely (`rand_clim_format`).

library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)

# This question was split-sampled - respondents did not all read the
# same thing - so this version is estimated on its own. Pooling the
# versions would average across the treatment.

# Read as character: a question asked in one wave is empty in the
# others, and a column empty for its first thousand rows is guessed
# logical, which turns every real value after it into NA.
wx22 <- read_csv("WX22_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

d <- bind_rows(
  wx22 |>
    filter(rand_clim_format == "10") |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      survey_year = "2022",
      resp = cond_risk_trust
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp), !is.na(PERSON_WEIGHT))

est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = 1, weights = PERSON_WEIGHT) |>
  group_by(survey_year, resp) |>
  summarise(p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
            .groups = "drop")

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("It would strongly reduce my trust",
                 "It would reduce my trust",
                 "It would have no effect on my trust",
                 "It would increase my trust",
                 "It would strongly increase my trust")
    ),
    survey_year = factor(
      survey_year,
      levels = c("2022")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp), fill = survey_year)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
                position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "Forecasters do the best they can, but sometimes they",
      "underestimate or overestimate the probability that a storm",
      "system will cause a tornado. We are interested in how these",
      "miscalculations might influence your trust in future",

      "more likely. As the day progresses, imagine that you see",
      "some rain and lightning, but the storm does not produce a",
      "tornado with 25 miles of your residence. How would this",
      "influence your trust in future forecasts?"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Survey year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
